scope_note: Everything under *.payflows.io plus vendor-hosted infra that runs their code or stores their data. Subdomain list in subdomains.txt. Known stack: VueJS front-end; AWS (S3, CloudFront, Lambda, API Gateway WebSocket, Cognito User Pool + Identity Pool eu-west-1:d1d858d9-a60d-456e-9321-0745dacfac45) for infra; Unleash feature flags; internal PyPI mirror. GitHub source is fully private.
ruled_out: Public GitHub org has any code - github.com/payflows is held but has zero public repos and zero public members
DockerHub org 'payflows' or variants - all 404, search returns 0 results
NPM user 'payflows' or packages matching 'payflows'/'payflows.io' - registry search total=0
PyPI user 'payflows' or packages 'payflows', 'payflows-core', 'payflows-sdk', 'payflows-client', 'luigi-payflows', 'pyflows-io' - all 404; 'mystix' and 'fawkes' exist but belong to unrelated authors
Leaked secrets on public GitHub (AKIA, DATABASE_URL, firebase, supabase, .env + payflows) - 0 Payflows-SAS-scoped hits
Commits authored or committed from @payflows.io on public repos - 0 (search_commits)
Any new subdomains discoverable via GitHub - 0; all URLs in the only public reference (api-evangelist/payflows) are already in subdomains.txt
Public GitHub Actions workflows exposing OIDC trust / cloud account IDs - no public repos, cannot inspect

pypi.payflows.io S3 bucket enumeration - origin bucket is 'payflows-pypi' in eu-west-1; ListObjectsV2/policy/acl/versioning all 403 AccessDenied, no s3-website config, no public index.html / robots.txt / simple/ / packages/ or any guessed package path (50+ probes, all NoSuchKey). Bucket name is leaked by standard S3 PermanentRedirect XML which is expected CloudFront+S3 behavior and not reportable on its own. Full probe log in raw/pypi/NOTES.md.

luigi-public-ws.payflows.io / luigi-api-public-ws.payflows.io direct WS compromise - both are AWS API Gateway WebSocket endpoints; only path '/' reaches the application; every WS Upgrade is intercepted by a Python Lambda authorizer that demands conversation_id (UUID) + token (JWT with kid-based JWKS lookup); 616 probes across 14 paths x 11 subprotocols produced zero 101 handshakes; see F001. No unauth data access, no introspection, no object-ID queries reachable. One low-sev info-disclosure logged (F001). Non-public counterparts luigi-ws / luigi-api-ws gate at the API Gateway itself with SigV4; no application reached.

scim.payflows.io SCIM 2.0 unauth enumeration - every /scim/v2/* path returns well-formed SCIM 401 'Unauthorized'. Auth bypass variants ruled out: Bearer null/undefined/empty/test, Basic admin:admin, X-API-Key, X-Forwarded-User, X-Amzn-Oidc-Identity, X-Original-URL path override, OPTIONS CORS, filter query pre-auth, .search POST, v1/path variants. No authorizer leak like F001. See raw/scim/NOTES.md. Reachable only with a provisioned SCIM bearer (SCIM clients are server-to-server integration partners).

payments-prod-docker-lambda / payments-dev-docker-lambda / luigi-prod-docker-lambda / luigi-dev-docker-lambda - all three return 'healthy' on /ping but nothing beyond. luigi-prod reaches a Flask/FastAPI 404 on every probed path with CORS Origin-reflection but no Access-Control-Allow-Credentials and no sensitive data route reachable; others sit behind API Gateway with MissingAuthenticationToken. Noted as a sub-observation in F003 rather than a separate finding.

balance-bot / balance / bot / balance-bot-dev subdomains - NXDOMAIN (confirmed by proxy 502-retry + direct curl 'Could not resolve host'). balance-bot is internal-only; does not have a public DNS record. Mentioned in F003 as new-service recon lead but not reachable from the public internet.

api.payflows.io micro-service gateway and workflow.payflows.io - all 14 enumerated services (connector, mystix, fawkes, bouncer, intake, audit-trail, payments, notification, counterparty, erp, approval, luigi, agents, accounting) return 403 Forbidden at the API Gateway on root path and common probe paths. Endpoint map extracted from app.payflows.io/assets/PfPopin-Bd8a5PJI.js and saved in raw/luigi/cur-pfpopin.js. intake.payflows.io direct (same Flask/FastAPI pattern as luigi-prod-docker-lambda: /health returns 200 'status: healthy', CORS Origin-reflection but no ACAC, no data route reachable). Unauth gateway surface is tight.

storybook.payflows.io - Basic auth tight. Did not match admin/admin, payflows/payflows, test/test, or storybook/storybook. Did not brute-force per Claude.md. Only reachable with a Payflows-provisioned Basic cred.

Would open: Luigi WS cross-tenant IDOR on conversation_id, SCIM /Users with the Cognito JWT, mass-assignment on PATCH /me, GraphQL introspection + walk, every /api/* micro-service listed in raw/luigi/cur-pfpopin.js.

open_threads.name: Passive-DNS feed for api.payflows.io ALB origin
open_threads.why: Current CT + Hackertarget passes only returned CloudFront IPs. SecurityTrails / VirusTotal passive DNS might show historic ALB / EC2 origin IPs. Direct-origin access bypasses CloudFront+WAF per Claude.md. Low expected payoff on a mature AWS deployment but cheap to try.

pending_decisions: Luigi WS post-auth exploration requires a valid Cognito JWT. Self-signup is blocked by a PreSignUp Lambda keyed on email domain (see F002); only tenants with autosignup enabled accept a new user, and the attacker's email domain must match. User-supplied peter.bjorn75@gmail.com cannot be used. Options: (a) ask Payflows to provision a sandbox tenant test account; (b) switch to another thread.

F003 includes an observation that a user-controlled appName value lands unsanitised in Unleash Prometheus labels (a Qualys scanner payload is persisted). Pursuing the write side (POST /api/client/register with a controlled appName) would be a mutation and is deferred to the account-availability decision.

findings.summary: Public Luigi WS Lambda authorizer leaks Python exception strings ('badly formed hexadecimal UUID string', "'kid'", 'Public key not found in jwks.json') and the full pre-auth model to any unauthenticated client.

findings.endpoint: POST https://cognito-idp.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/ (X-Amz-Target: SignUp) against 7 Payflows app clients
findings.summary: PreSignUp Lambda returns verbatim exception 'Could not retrieve tenant from domain name or tenant does not authorize autosignup' to anonymous clients, disclosing that signup is gated by email-domain -> tenant resolution and a per-tenant autosignup flag. Second instance of the F001 pattern on a different Lambda.

findings.endpoint: GET https://unleash.payflows.io/internal-backstage/prometheus and GET https://unleash.payflows.io/docs/openapi.json (same instance mirrored at ff.payflows.io)
findings.summary: Unauthenticated 3929-line Prometheus dump and 158-path OpenAPI spec on the Unleash feature-flag server leaks Unleash 7.0.3, PostgreSQL 15.13, 17 licensed users, 142 feature toggles, project 'default', envs production/development, internal appNames (incl. 'balance-bot', 'Help.Applications.Contributors' not in subdomains.txt), evidence of past public-signup invites being used, and a persisted stored-input artefact ('<script>alert(qualysxss)</script>' as appName) proving an unauth sink into Prometheus labels unsanitised.
